supersedes.why: That file was recorded before the aligned-artifact tier landed (ds4 78471cb/64a3b81). It reports cuda_allocation_gib 12.70 with the model read in place from the file mapping, so its 'no GPU tool shows the model footprint' conclusion no longer applies: on this build the weights are CUDA-owned and nvtop reports them. It is left in the tree untouched as the record of that earlier configuration.
supersedes.status: untracked, not modified by this run

residency.kv_detail: 12 full-attention layers hold the whole context; 36 sliding layers are fixed at a 128-token window (18 MiB total)

observed_under_load.note: sampled while a 33068-token cold prefill was in flight

tooling_caveats: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used reports [N/A] on GB10; use nvtop -s.
nvtop's per-process field is gpu_mem_bytes_alloc. There is no gpu_memory_usage key in this nvtop (3.3.2) JSON.
Process VmRSS understates residency: ds4 leaves the 85.56 GiB model mmap unpinned and hands the pages to the CUDA cache, so most of the footprint is CUDA-owned rather than process-anonymous.
A small-context run is not comparable to a 256K run: two 127-token sessions peak near 90.17 GiB, the 256K server at 103.62 GiB, and the difference is almost entirely the 12.02 GiB KV.
After a clean process exit the 595.71.05 driver may hold the unified allocation. nvtop showing no process is not proof that system memory came back.
